question: Does the retained first-party reversal characteristic shape provide a visible, gamut-safe and non-gamma photographic tone mechanism on a rights-cleared camera-diverse population?

operator.curve_compile: for each frozen channel trace compute T=10^-D, normalize exact first/last T to 0/1, average the three normalized transmissions, and PCHIP on normalized traced log-exposure position
operator.application_domain: CIELAB L-star only; a-star/b-star initially unchanged
operator.input_coordinate: L-star / 100, explicitly a generic display-look coordinate rather than scene or film exposure
operator.gamut_execution: existing source-segment linear-sRGB gamut compression with 24 iterations

controls.best_gamma: one per-image bounded gamma fitted on the exact colour-metric sample to candidate L-star; diagnostic basic-tone control
controls.source_boundary: new epsilon boundary relative to source

stop_rules: Do not change trace, transmittance normalization, strength, colour domain, source population, gamma control, gamut executor or gates after candidate pixels are scored.
Any automatic or confirmed severe-artifact failure closes this exact generic characteristic-look compiler without strength, coordinate, curve, source or threshold rescue.

Pass may retain a generic film-inspired tone mechanism for a fresh comparison with the incumbent; it cannot establish Velvia calibration, scene exposure, dye colour, scanner/process truth or product promotion.
claim_ceiling: Rights-cleared photographic development evidence for a generic tone mechanism compiled from a retained first-party reversal characteristic shape; not Velvia calibration, stock colour, scene exposure, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
